Assessment of the lock-ordering structural test specifically: it is a genuine structural check, not a vacuous one. It reads the real lib/letflow/engine.ex source text at test time (File.read!), isolates run_cancel_instance/5's own Multi body via String.split on the function's own signature and the following '# M1 --' comment marker (bounding the search to just this function, not able to false-match some unrelated :open_tasks/:timer_cancellations/:instance_projection, text elsewhere in the file), and asserts the byte-offset ordering of the three step-name atoms via :binary.match/2. This is exactly the kind of check that is unobservable via any single-process behavioral assertion (a lock-ordering deadlock-avoidance property) and my own mutation reproduction confirms it is the only test in the file sensitive to the step's position -- it earns its place rather than being redundant with test 10's rollback-behavior test.
